fragment: This paper presents a comprehensive spectro-temporal investigation of the low-mass X-ray binary (LMXB) neutron star atoll source GX 9+9, based on a single archival AstroSat observation (Obs. ID: A09_018T01_9000003774) taken on July 25, 2020. Utilizing both the Large Area X-ray Proportional Counter (LAXPC) and Soft X-ray Telescope (SXT) instruments, the authors determined that GX 9+9 was in the soft/banana state (BS) with a disk-dominating energy spectrum between 0.7–25.0 keV. The flux was segregated into three levels (FL1: 450–570 cts/s; FL2: 570–650 cts/s; FL3: 650–770 cts/s) for flux-resolved spectral analysis. The best-fit spectral model was const*tbabs*(thcomp*diskbb), combining SXT and LAXPC data with 90% confidence level constraints. The source exhibited an average estimated inner-disk radius (Rin) of 16.57 ± 1.29 km (or 16.54 ± 1.78 km in the conclusion), consistent with prior estimates despite different distance and inclination assumptions. Total unabsorbed flux ranged from 5.94 × 10⁻⁹ to 7.30 × 10⁻⁹ ergs s⁻¹ cm⁻² over 0.01–100 keV, showing an increase across flux levels. In the temporal domain, LAXPC data revealed broad-band noise (BBN) centered at ~0.1 Hz, fitted with two Lorentzians; no QPOs were detected. Energy-dependent modeling using the Garg et al. propagative model formalism (reduced χ² ≈ 0.80) attributed the variability to simultaneous changes in the inner-disk temperature (δkTin ≈ 0.56 ± 0.10%) and fractional scattering (δfs ≈ 81 ± 32%), with a positive phase lag of 0.11 ± 0.08, indicating that perturbations propagate from the inner disk toward the coronal region.

fragment: This paper introduces Dense-TSNet, an ultra-lightweight speech enhancement network designed for resource-constrained edge devices. Motivated by the observation that single-channel speech enhancement models with approximately 10,000 parameters are under-researched, the authors propose a novel Dense Two-Stage (Dense-TS) architecture that replaces dilated convolutions in the classic Two-Stage structure with densely connected Two-Stage modules to smooth the loss landscape of narrow lightweight models. The network incorporates a Multi-View Gaze Block (MVGB) composed of a Large Kernel Extractor (LKE), Learnable-Sigmoid Gate (LSG), and Channel Attention (CA), all implemented entirely with CNNs for efficient deployment. The model processes only the magnitude spectrum of the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) input. A significant contribution is the Consistency Magnitude Loss, which computes the minimum distance between the magnitude spectrum of twice-STFTed speech and the clean speech magnitude spectrum, avoiding complex-domain computations that lightweight models struggle to fit. Ablation studies on the VoiceBank+DEMAND dataset demonstrate that the MVGB components (LKE, CA, LSG) each contribute substantially to PESQ scores, with the full configuration achieving 3.05 PESQ, 4.51 CSIG, 3.58 CBAK, and 3.86 COVL. Comparisons reveal that Dense-TSNet achieves 3.05 PESQ with only 14,000 parameters—the first speech enhancement model at approximately 10K parameters—outperforming the classic TS baseline (2.96 PESQ) despite a narrower architecture. Further loss function studies reveal that while adding a Metric Loss (via PESQ discriminator) increases the PESQ score (up to 3.41 at P=200), it also increases spectral errors and introduces pseudohallucination distortions, leading the authors to default to only Consistency Magnitude Loss. The final model uses 14,000 parameters and 356M MACs, making it uniquely suited for deployment on smartphones and cameras.

fragment: This paper introduces Dense-TSNet, an ultra-lightweight speech enhancement network designed for resource-constrained edge devices. Motivated by the observation that single-channel speech enhancement models with approximately 10,000 parameters are under-researched, the authors propose a novel Dense Two-Stage (Dense-TS) architecture that replaces dilated convolutions in the classic Two-Stage structure with densely connected Two-Stage modules to smooth the loss landscape of narrow lightweight models. The network incorporates a Multi-View Gaze Block (MVGB) composed of a Large Kernel Extractor (LKE), Learnable-Sigmoid Gate (LSG), and Channel Attention (CA), all implemented entirely with CNNs for efficient deployment. The model processes only the magnitude spectrum of the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) input. A significant contribution is the Consistency Magnitude Loss, which computes the minimum distance between the magnitude spectrum of twice-STFTed speech and the clean speech magnitude spectrum, avoiding complex-domain computations that lightweight models struggle to fit. Ablation studies on the VoiceBank+DEMAND dataset demonstrate that the MVGB components (LKE, CA, LSG) each contribute substantially to PESQ scores, with the full configuration achieving 3.05 PESQ, 4.51 CSIG, 3.58 CBAK, and 3.86 COVL. Comparisons reveal that Dense-TSNet achieves 3.05 PESQ with only 14,000 parameters—the first speech enhancement model at approximately 10K parameters—outperforming the classic TS baseline (2.96 PESQ) despite a narrower architecture. Further loss function studies reveal that while adding a Metric Loss (via PESQ discriminator) increases the PESQ score (up to 3.41 at P=200), it also increases spectral errors and introduces pseudohallucination distortions, leading the authors to default to only Consistency Magnitude Loss. The final model uses 14,000 parameters and 356M MACs, making it uniquely suited for deployment on smartphones and cameras.

fragment: This paper introduces Recurrent Interpolants for Probabilistic Time Series Prediction, a novel framework that blends the computational efficiency of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with the high-quality probabilistic modeling of stochastic interpolants (SI), a generalization of diffusion and flow-based models. Standard probabilistic time series forecasting methods, such as RNNs or transformer-based models with parametric output layers, are limited by simple probability families, while generative approaches like diffusion or flow matching suffer from scalability issues because model size depends on both feature dimension and time window length. The authors extend the theory of stochastic interpolants to a conditional generation framework with extra control features, enabling the model to learn a joint distribution p(x_{t+1}, x_t | x_{t-P:t-1}) where x_t is the current observation, x_{t+1} is the prediction target, and x_{t-P:t-1} is the context window. An RNN encodes the context into a history prompt h_t, which condition the velocity and score functions of the SI module. The model is trained on 3-tuples (x_{t+1}, x_t, x_{t-P:t-1}) and inference proceeds by transporting x_t to x_{t+1} via a forward SDE. On synthetic 2D datasets (Circles, Moons, Rings, Swissroll, 8gaussians), SI achieves Wasserstein distances ranging from 0.007 to 0.359 across variants. On real-world multivariate datasets (Solar, Exchange, Traffic, Wiki), SI outperforms or matches DDPM, SGM, and FM-based baselines on three out of four tasks under the CRPS-sum metric, demonstrating competitive probabilistic forecasting capability. The authors also compare against Vec-LSTM, showing that generative modeling of the probability distribution is critical for large-dimension time series prediction.

fragment: This paper presents a comprehensive physico-chemical and electrochemical characterization of highly concentrated aqueous binary CH₃COOK/CH₃COONa electrolytes, targeting the development of water-in-salt (WISE) electrolytes for sodium-ion batteries. The authors prepared four binary solutions with a fixed CH₃COOK concentration of 20 mol kg⁻¹ and varying CH₃COONa concentrations (1, 2.5, 5, and 7 mol kg⁻¹), alongside a 1 M NaAc control. The series was characterized via Differential Scanning Calorimetry (-120 to 90 °C), rheology (viscosity vs. temperature), electrical impedance spectroscopy (conductivity), and linear sweep voltammetry (electrochemical stability window). Thermal analysis revealed that glass transition temperature (Tg) increases with salt concentration, correlating with the transition from salt-in-water to water-in-salt behavior; notably, the 7N20K composition (7 mol kg⁻¹ NaAc + 20 mol kg⁻¹ KAc) showed a low liquidus temperature (~0 °C), suggesting resistance to salt crystallization. Ionic conductivity followed Vogel-Tamman-Fulcher behavior across all compositions, with the most concentrated 7N20K solution maintaining 21.2 mS cm⁻¹ at 25 °C, comparable to organic-based systems. Rheological data classified the acetates as structure-making salts with Arrhenius viscosity-temperature dependence. Electrochemical stability window measurements showed suppression of hydrogen evolution at higher concentrations, with 7N20K reaching 3 V in ideal flooded-cell conditions. As a proof-of-concept, carbon-coated LiTi₂(PO₄)₃ (CLTP) NASICON was synthesized via a one-pot sol-gel route and cycled in 7N20K electrolyte vs. 1 M NaAc. CLTP demonstrated reversible Na⁺ insertion at -0.7 V vs. SHE with 85 mAh g⁻¹ first-cycle anodic capacity, 96% average charge efficiency, and 90% capacity retention over 60 cycles. Impedance spectroscopy revealed a low charge-transfer activation energy of 0.12 eV and a diffusion coefficient of ~10⁻¹³ cm² s⁻¹ at room temperature, confirming the kinetic feasibility of the NASICON/WISE interface for sodium-ion battery applications.

fragment: This paper reports the 30-step enantioselective total synthesis of madangamine E, a complex pentacyclic marine natural product, enabled by a novel organocatalytic desymmetrization reaction. The key transformation involves an intramolecular Michael addition of a prochiral 4-aminocyclohexanone-linked β,β'-disubstituted nitroolefin to a tethered nitroolefin, catalyzed by a bifunctional primary amine thiourea organocatalyst. This reaction concurrently establishes three stereogenic centers, including a quaternary carbon, in near-perfect enantio- and diastereo-selectivity (99% ee as single diastereomer). The catalytic cycle was computationally probed using DFT, revealing a cooperative push/pull mechanism stabilized by multiple hydrogen bonding interactions between the thiourea, nitro group, and enamine moieties. The synthetic sequence proceeds from commercially available 1,4-cyclohexanedione monoethylene acetal, constructs the bicyclic core via the desymmetrization, and completes the pentacyclic skeleton through oxidative lactamization, a two-step Z-selective olefination of a sterically hindered ketone, and two ring-closing metathesis (RCM) macrocyclizations. The study demonstrates that early catalytic desymmetrization can install all stereochemical information in a complex natural product, and the pathway was validated by X-ray diffraction and DFT. The scalability of the desymmetrization was demonstrated on a 5g scale, and the model nitroolefin was accessible on a 17g scale, supporting the practical utility of the strategy.

fragment: This study investigates the dielectric response of molecular-scale nanocomposites comprising silver (Ag) inclusions embedded in a magnesium oxide (MgO) matrix, focusing on how nanoparticle morphology—size, shape, and orientation relative to an external field—tunes the dielectric permittivity. Using Car-Parinello Molecular Dynamics (CPMD) and the Modern Theory of Polarization implemented in Quantum Espresso (versions 6.0 and 6.6), the authors model polarization in eight Ag-MgO systems (three rod-like and five disk-like inclusions) with sizes ranging from 8 to 32 atoms. Key findings reveal that dielectric permittivity enhancements of 30-100% are achievable with inclusion sizes of 8 to 32 atoms. Multi-layer disk-like inclusions (disks 332, 432, 442) yield more than 70% enhancement in ε_r over the matrix permittivity at similar volume loadings, significantly outperforming rod-like counterparts. The mechanism is attributed to local field enhancements at the Ag-MgO interface: electrons in the silver nanoparticle polarize and shift charge density to the interface, creating induced electrostatic fields in the matrix. The 'reach' and intensity of these induced fields depend strongly on the nanoparticle's orientation—parallel alignment maximizes the effective polarizability while perpendicular alignment induces depolarization regions that can suppress the overall dielectric response. The Born effective charge tensor is used to map local charge density variations, revealing that the strongest interfacial effects are confined to within 3 angstroms of the inclusion edge. The study concludes that molecular-scale metal inclusions, due to their finite size and quantum nature, avoid the percolation and tunneling issues of bulk metallic nanoparticles while providing a tunable platform for high-κ dielectrics. The authors note that 2D nanoparticles (421, 441) show a decrease in polarization relative to the bulk in both directions because electrons are confined in the z-direction. Future directions include other matrix materials (SiO₂, HfO₂), diverse transition metal inclusions, and exploration of the perpendicular response limits.

fragment: This study demonstrates the application of the subgroup-discovery (SGD) artificial-intelligence approach to a hybrid experimental-plus-theoretical dataset to identify physicochemical design rules for selective oxidation catalysts. The authors synthesized and tested 120 SiO2-supported catalysts containing ruthenium (Ru), tungsten (W), and phosphorus (P) in the catalytic oxidation of propylene. DFT-calculated free-atom properties, combined with reaction temperature, served as 11 candidate descriptive parameters. The oxygenates yield (acrolein and acrylic acid) was used as the target in SGD. The identified SG rules—defining constraints on temperature (280 ≤ T ≤ 300 °C), phosphorus content (JK > 0.55), and composition-weighted electronegativity (3.910 ≤ VY < 4.002 eV)—isolated a subgroup comprising only 1.2% of the data (15 out of 1220 measurements) yielding an average oxygenates yield of 24.15%, five times the global average of 4.83%. These rules were subsequently used to design and test four-component (Ru-W-P-V) and five-component (Ru-W-P-Te-V) catalysts. The four-component Ru-W-P-Te catalyst achieved 60.19% yield, and the five-component Ru-W-P-Te-Ta catalyst achieved 59.60%, both nearly double the highest training yield of 26.85%. A second SGD on the four- and five-component data (746 points) yielded new rules: T ≥ 360 °C, LA+1 ≤ 1.001 Å, and VH < -1.593 eV. The study concludes that SGD can identify interpretable, chemically meaningful rules for exceptional catalytic performance that extend beyond the training data to substantially more complex and performant material compositions.

fragment: This study reports a free-solvent, mechanochemical synthesis method for producing calcium phosphate bioceramics (potassium calcium phosphates) as eco-friendly soil conditioners, repurposing eggshell waste (calcite) and potassium dihydrogen phosphate (KH2PO4). Based on reverse logistics principles, the process applies mechanical energy via high-energy ball milling to drive a solid-state chemical reaction between eggshell waste and KH2PO4 without solvents or unwanted subproducts. XRD analysis identifies the formation of K3CaH(PO4)2 (PDF 22-1218) and CaKPO4 (PDF 33-1002) phases, with the transformation confirmed by TGA, DSC, and 31P NMR MAS. Solubility kinetics in 2% citric acid reveal that the milled phosphates delay the release of potassium and phosphorus compared to the KH2PO4 precursor, while simultaneously increasing the bioavailability of calcium relative to the CaCO3 precursor. Soil release essays confirm these findings: the 2 h/600 rpm sample achieved 45 mg/kg P release at 30 days (15% of total P), compared to 40% release for the KH2PO4 precursor, and demonstrated an intermediate P radial diffusion (22% slower than KH2PO4, 34% faster than struvite). Further, hydroxyapatite (Ca10(PO4)6(OH)2) formation was observed in situ, yielding 30.97 mg/kg bioavailable Ca at 30 days. The authors conclude that the mechanochemical bioceramic acts as a smart release fertilizer providing superior nutrient management for P, K, and Ca simultaneously.

fragment: This study reports the design and synthesis of a series of star-shaped aromatic nitric acid radicals (ANARs) that achieve highly efficient photothermal conversion via restricted radiative decay. The authors developed four radical species—TPA-TPA-O6, TPA-TPZ-O6, TPA-PY-O8, and Spiro-O8—synthesized via facile demethylation and air-oxidation of phenolic hydroxyl precursors without steric hindrance protection. These open-shell organic conjugated radicals exhibit rich resonance structures, including closed-shell nitro-like and open-shell nitroxide states with unpaired electrons delocalized across conjugated backbones, imparting both electrochemical and thermal stability. Characterization by UV-Vis-NIR, ESR, cyclic voltammetry (CV), and PLQY revealed that the demethylated radicals exhibit extremely high spin concentration (confirmed by ESR) and drastically reduced photoluminescence quantum yields (<1%, compared to moderate PLQY in methoxy precursors), indicating dominant nonradiative decay channels. The TPA-TPA-O6 variant demonstrated a black powder color with broadband absorption extending from 300 to 2000 nm in aggregated state, significantly red-shifted compared to its precursor. Under 808 nm laser irradiation at 0.8 W cm⁻², TPA-TPA-O6 temperature rose from 25 °C to ~210 °C within 60 s, exhibiting superior photothermal stability over ten cycles. In an interfacial evaporation system on PU foam, TPA-TPA-O6 achieved a solar-to-vapor efficiency of 89.41% and a water evaporation rate of 1.293 kg m⁻² h⁻¹ under 1 sun (1.0 kW m⁻²), representing top performance among pure organic small molecule photothermal materials. The system was further validated for seawater desalination, reducing all four primary ions below membrane-based method values. The study demonstrates that neutral, stable organic radical small molecules with high spin concentration provide a new design strategy for solar energy materials with low cost, simple synthesis, and competitive performance to inorganic or conjugated polymer alternatives.

fragment: This study reports a sustainable, metal-free photocatalytic oxidative coupling (POC) of arylamines to azoaromatics at the charged aqueous interfaces (CAIs) of micelles, achieving up to 100% yield and 100% selectivity under ambient air atmosphere. The methodology utilizes Eosin Y (EY) as a low-cost organic photocatalyst and K3PO4 as a base, with 0.6 mol% PC required, outperforming previous Ir-based organic photocatalyst methodologies. The system operates with fast kinetics (4 hours for 100% conversion) at λ = 525 nm and a broad substrate scope encompassing 8 electron-rich and electron-deficient arylamines. The remarkable catalytic boosting is attributed to two synergistic effects: (1) non-diffusive photoinduced electron transfer (PET) with an ultrafast time constant of 0.3 ps, and (2) modulation of redox potentials at the micellar interface. The micellar scaffold (CTAB at 40 mM) serves as an efficient assembly that solubilizes both the cationic EY and the hydrophobic arylamines in close proximity at the Stern layer. The reaction mechanism proceeds via amine radical formation followed by bimolecular coupling, with atmospheric O2 acting as a sacrificial oxidant regenerated as H2O2. Fluorescence quenching experiments with linear Stern-Volmer plots (kq = 6.3 × 10^12 M^-1 s^-1) confirm non-diffusive PET, and BHT radical trapping experiments corroborate the radical pathway. The work constitutes the first report on aqueous-phase synthesis of azo compounds under ambient conditions, opening new directions for sustainable azoaromatic synthesis.

fragment: This paper presents a universal post-preparation method to enhance photoluminescence (PL) intensity in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) by coating them with paraffin, a simple hydrocarbon. Previously, PL enhancement strategies were compound-specific: sulfur-based TMDCs (MoS2, WS2) benefited from p-type dopants (F4TCNQ) or superacids (TFSI), while selenium-based TMDCs (MoSe2, WSe2) had very limited strategies. The authors demonstrate that coating monolayer MoS2, WS2, MoSe2, and WSe2 with paraffin—which has a high thermal expansion coefficient—induces spontaneous fluctuation, strain, and eventual desorption of the monolayer from the substrate due to paraffin penetration. This removes the substrate effect, a key factor suppressing PL. Quantitative results show PL enhancement factors of 215× for MoS2, 55× for WS2, 9× for WSe2, and 50× for MoSe2 relative to as-exfoliated flakes. Raman spectroscopy confirms in-plane strain (E′ peak shift -0.72 cm⁻¹ average) and carrier concentration reduction (A′ peak shift +1.03 cm⁻¹). Optical microscopy captures the time-dependent deformation into wrinkled or bundled structures. The method is universal, works on both sulfur- and selenium-based TMDCs, and leverages paraffin's insulative, flexible, and transparent properties for optoelectronic applications. The authors propose that the combined effects of strain from paraffin's thermal expansion and subsequent desorption drive the PL enhancement. The method is applicable to other 2D layered materials as well.

fragment: This study reports the successful continuous partial oxidation of methane to methanol and acetic acid at atmospheric pressure using a modified silica-supported bimetallic (Au-Fe) catalyst with 15% w/v H2O2 as the oxidant. The authors address the long-standing 'holy grail' problem of methane-to-methanol (M2M) conversion by operating under benign conditions—atmospheric pressure and mild temperatures (80 °C)—rather than the high-pressure, high-temperature conditions typically required for methane activation. The catalyst, designated AuFeHS, is prepared via a modified deposition precipitation method onto hydrophobic silica (HS), a sodium-containing silica support modified during synthesis. The catalyst features atomic clusters of Fe (0.46 wt %) and Au nanoparticles (0.23 wt %, 1.3–3.0 nm) on HS. Key spectroscopic characterization (XPS, XANES, EXAFS, HRTEM, contact angle analysis, and in-situ IR) confirms: (1) the presence of low-valent Fe³⁻δ⁺ species, (2) cationic Auδ⁺ species (15% relative area), (3) atomic dispersion of Fe with no Fe-Fe interaction, (4) Au nanoparticles of 1.4–2.8 nm, and (5) hydrophobic surface (118° contact angle). In batch experiments at 10 bar CH4 and 20 bar total pressure, AuFeHS achieved 1666 mmol/(gFe+Au) methanol yield with 95% selectivity within 30 min. Co-feeding CO switched selectivity to acetic acid, yielding 3403 µmol/gcat within 1 h. In continuous flow at atmospheric pressure for 7 h, AuFeHS delivered 224 mmol/(gFe+Au) methanol yield (0.42 mol/(kg catalyst · h)) at 80 °C. Isotope labeling (CD4) confirmed that the methanol oxygenate originates from the methane substrate, not support degradation. The work surpasses previous high-pressure batch benchmarks (e.g., 0.081 mol/(kg catalyst · h) at 20 bar) while operating at atmospheric pressure, establishing a new benchmark for low-pressure methane activation.

fragment:
This study introduces a multi-step workflow for identifying and energetically ordering feasible crystal configurations of cubic Li7La3Zr2O12 (c-LLZO), a prominent solid-state electrolyte candidate whose ground-state Li occupancy has lacked consensus. The authors face a combinatorial explosion where populating 120 crystallographic sites with 56 Li atoms yields approximately 7.4 × 10^34 structures, rendering brute-force methods unviable. Their approach begins by eliminating structures with overlapping Li atoms using a 1.7 Å minimal distance cutoff—a value grounded in the crystal ionic diameter and validated against Li-dimer calculations. This geometric constraint reduces the configuration space to ~2.3 × 10^8 structures, which is further compressed to ~2 × 10^6 unique conformations using a combination of connectivity matrix flattening and Local Sensitive Hashing (LSH) for fast symmetry detection (O(N) scaling). 

Energetic ordering is achieved through a two-pronged approach: COMPASSIII force field calculations on the Li-sublattice and 1235 single-point DFT calculations using ONETEP with PBE functional, 830 eV cutoff. These DFT energies are mapped to a multiple linear regression (MLR) model using frequency occurrence lists of all Li-Li interactions as descriptors, achieving a correlation of 0.9996 on the test set. The study identifies four structures within 0.026 eV (1 kT at 298 K) of the lowest-energy configuration, all with an 8:48 24d:96h occupancy ratio. Geometry optimizations on these four structures confirm that the 96h-to-24d transition (occurring once) yielded the absolute lowest energy structure, 0.58 eV lower than the optimized single-point lowest. The authors conclude that many previously reported experimental and theoretical structures may be physically unfeasible under geometric constraints and provide all generated structures in a public database to improve reproducibility in c-LLZO research.

These DFT energies are mapped to a multiple linear regression (MLR) model using frequency occurrence lists of all Li-Li interactions as descriptors, achieving a correlation of 0.9996 on the test set. The study identifies four structures within 0.026 eV (1 kT at 298 K) of the lowest-energy configuration, all with an 8:48 24d:96h occupancy ratio. Geometry optimizations on these four structures confirm that the 96h-to-24d transition (occurring once) yielded the absolute lowest energy structure, 0.58 eV lower than the optimized single-point lowest. The authors conclude that many previously reported experimental and theoretical structures may be physically unfeasible under geometric constraints and provide all generated structures in a public database to improve reproducibility in c-LLZO research.

fragment: This Feature Article highlights recent advances in bioinspired supramolecular materials designed to mimic dynamic bio-interfaces essential for cellular activities such as adhesion, signal transduction, and substance transportation. The extracellular matrix (ECM), phospholipid bilayers, and membrane-embedded proteins are identified as key bio-interface components. The authors review several distinct material strategies: (1) Stiffness-controlled RADA-based peptide hydrogels (A16G and A16G-Ncad) that mimic ECM scaffold cells to promote neuronal migration in injured neonatal neocortex; (2) JigSAP peptide fibers with jigsaw-shaped hydrophobic surfaces that incorporate and sustained-release VEGF at 39 mol% over 168 hours, promoting angiogenesis in ischaemic stroke models; (3) Redox-responsive JigSAP-IMI and JigSAP-MII variants that undergo gel-sol transition upon H2O2 exposure; (4) DPPC/Chol-MBP/Cu phospholipid nanosheets stabilized by Cu2+-crosslinked peptide surfactants enabling extended blood circulation; and (5) GUVs functionalized with the photoresponsive molecular machine AzoMEx that induce endocytosis-like outside-in membrane fission for efficient encapsulation (22.6 × 10^11 virions/mL) and in vivo delivery of M13 phage viruses to multiple organs while retaining infectivity. Collectively, these supramolecular approaches demonstrate how bottom-up design of dynamic, stimuli-responsive materials can reconstruct biomimetic interfaces for regenerative medicine and drug delivery.

fragment: GUIDEMOL is a Python-based graphical user interface (GUI) application developed to provide accessible computing of molecular descriptors and 3D grid representations of molecular structures. Built upon the RDKit software library, GUIDEMOL targets chemoinformatics users, scientists, and students who possess varying levels of computer and programming skills. The application leverages the tkinter package—the standard Python interface to the Tcl/Tk GUI toolkit—to present a minimalist interface for routine chemoinformatics tasks. Key functionality includes: (1) calculation of molecular descriptors implemented in RDKit, such as RDF, MORSE, WHIM, AUTOCORR3D, GETAWAY, PEOE_VSA, and SMR_VSA; (2) generation of 3D molecular structures from SMILES using the MMFF94 force field with MMFFOptimizeMolecule; and (3) computation of 3D grid representations based on either electrostatic potential (EP) using Gasteiger or MMFF partial charges, or voxel encoding of atomic properties (atomic number, partial charge, molecular refractivity contributions, or logP contributions). The GUI incorporates various tkinter widgets (buttons, checkbuttons, radiobuttons, entries, labels, scrollbar) and uses the filedialog module for native file/directory selection. For users requiring automation or integration into pipelines, a command-line interface (CLI) is also provided for grid calculations. The source code is openly available under the three-clause BSD license, enabling commercial and non-commercial use. A noteworthy technical observation is that certain 3D descriptors (GETAWAY, MORSE, WHIM) exhibited non-deterministic behavior, producing different values across runs or operating systems within the same RDKit version (2022.9.5), exemplified by the structure generated for COc1ccc(cc1(OC))Br.

fragment: This work addresses the limitation of traditional linearized kinetic analysis (Tafel and reactant order dependence) in electrocatalysis, which assumes simple rate equations can be decoupled and linearized on log-log plots—a strategy that fails when surface coverage effects, mixed rate control, or electrolyte poisoning are present. The authors introduce a robotic platform that automates the sequential testing of up to ten electrochemical cells, each with potentially different electrodes, electrolytes, gas-phase compositions, and voltages, enabling cohesive kinetic analysis over wide reaction condition ranges. The system was applied to CO2 electroreduction to CO at three immobilized metal tetrapyrroles: cobalt phthalocyanine (CoPc), cobalt tetraphenylporphyrin (CoTPP), and iron phthalocyanine (FePc). The cohesive kinetic analysis revealed that CoPc and CoTPP exhibit voltage-dependent bicarbonate inhibition: the apparent bicarbonate order is most negative at less reductive potentials and becomes positive at more reductive potentials, consistent with models of bicarbonate poisoning combined with potential-dependent mixed control. In contrast, FePc shows greater bicarbonate inhibition at more reductive potentials, a trend explained by a mechanism where the most abundant reactive intermediate precedes the unoccupied site, causing coverage of the poisoning species to increase despite the local poisoning equilibrium shift. CO2 order dependences were also non-ideal: CoPc showed near-ideal first-order dependence, CoTPP showed slightly sub-unity order decreasing at more reductive potentials (consistent with surface saturation), and FePc exhibited the most unusual behavior where voltage inhibited the reaction at low CO2 partial pressures, captured by a mixed-control model with an on-cycle poisoning species. These findings demonstrate that complex reaction mechanisms, not amenable to standard linearization, are prevalent across this class of electrocatalysts, and that automation provides a robust pathway to interrogate them.

fragment: This paper presents the first direct experimental visualization of a π-hole—a π-electron-deficient cavity in a halogen-substituted polyaromatic hydrocarbon—on a single molecule using Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM). The authors investigate 9,10-dichlorooctafluoroanthracene (FCl-An) and compare it to anthracene (An) on an Au(111) surface. The π-hole concept, previously predicted only theoretically, is confirmed by KPFM imaging that reveals a characteristic bow-tie pattern in the local contact potential difference (LCPD) map of FCl-An, which is absent in An. Noncontact atomic force microscopy (nc-AFM) with a CO-functionalized tip was used to structurally resolve the self-assembled rhombic periodic molecular island (one An and two FCl-An molecules per unit cell), with DFT calculations providing a benchmark that unambiguously assigns molecular identities. KPFM imaging, performed with the same CO-terminated tip, captured submolecular LCPD variations that match simulated maps generated from DFT-calculated electrostatic potential maps. Furthermore, specific-site force-distance spectroscopy revealed a 30 pm height difference between An (330 pm) and FCl-An (360 pm) above the Au(111) surface, attributed to the π-hole increasing the ionization potential and suppressing charge induction at the molecule/metal interface. SAPT0 energy decomposition confirmed that while dispersion dominates, the induction energy is significantly larger for An than for FCl-An. This work establishes KPFM as a viable tool for real-space submolecular charge distribution imaging and demonstrates that π-holes fundamentally alter non-covalent electrostatic interactions, affecting both molecular self-assembly and surface adsorption properties.

fragment: This work presents the first machine learning force field (MLFF) ranking of candidate solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) structures formed in lithium-ion batteries, combining organic and inorganic components that pose significant simulation challenges. The authors develop a multitask QRNN (Quaternion Recurrent Neural Network) model trained simultaneously on both hybrid (wB97X-D3BJ/def2-TZVPD) and pure (PBE-D3) DFT reference labels, complemented by an organic chemistry dataset (SPICE) to broaden chemical coverage. Data generation employs multiple rounds of active learning enhanced by Artificial Force Induced Reactions (AFIR) and Nudged Elastic Band (NEB) on the QRNN potential energy surface, alongside OPLS4 molecular dynamics with reaction templates in a 1 M LiPF6 in EC solution system. The model is trained with hidden layers of size 256, 224, and 192 across elements, using the Adamax optimizer with decoupled weight decay and a learning rate of 2e-3. The methodology extends prior QRNN applications to complex redox-reactive metalorganic systems, producing stable MD dynamics at 400 K and 1000 atm. The model identifies four sets of candidate SEI structures with 5, 12, 23, and 33 added Li+ ions per box, ranked by mean potential energy over 20 ps MD trajectories. The most lithiated subgroup (33 Li+) is validated against the best available surface reaction energy barriers from Table 1, though experimental metrics like density and diffusivity are unavailable. Statistical bonding analysis reveals that P-F and Li-O bonds correlate with lower energies (more stable structures), while C-O and Li-F bonds correlate with higher energies. The paper emphasizes that this multitask QRNN framework can capture complex reactions characteristic of an SEI and proposes extending the work to multiple electrolyte formulations for property prediction. The authors conclude that while the model is not yet final, it establishes a quantitative baseline for understanding Li-ion battery interphases and sets a foundation for future MLFF-based SEI optimization.

fragment: This study investigates the insecticidal potential of crude and purified extracts from Ajuga iva (Lamiaceae) against Spodoptera littoralis, a major pest of cotton, maize, and rice. The authors exploited the presence of phytoecdysteroids—steroid analogs that mimic insect molting hormones—and clerodane diterpenes in A. iva to test green pest management alternatives to synthetic insecticides. Using a combination of larval feeding bioassays, LC-TOF-MS identification, TLC profiling, fluorescence microscopy of gut histology, and weight gain monitoring, the team demonstrated that A. iva crude leaf extract (50-250 µg/µl) significantly increases mortality in both first-instar (25%, 65%, 85%) and third-instar larvae, reduces larval weight gain, suppresses relative growth rate, and prevents successful pupation. A fractionated mixture of three phytoecdysteroids (20-hydroxyecdysone, makisterone A, and cyasterone) was also shown to elicit similar toxic effects. Histological analysis revealed that the extracts cause smaller, abnormally shaped nuclei and reduced actin filament density in larval guts, suggesting direct physiological damage. The study concludes that A. iva phytoecdysteroids and clerodanes offer a promising botanical control agent for S. littoralis, supporting integrated pest management programs with reduced environmental risk compared to traditional insecticides.

fragment: This study investigates the relationship between Article Processing Charges (APC), Impact Factor (IF), Eigen Factor (EF), citability, and publisher country within the ecosystem of Golden Open Access (GOA) natural science journals. The author collected and cleaned metadata from the Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ), starting with a pool of 14,275 records, and filtered for 237 GOA natural science journals after excluding medical and engineering journals with IF > 40. Statistical analysis using Pearson's correlation confirmed that APC is significantly and positively correlated with IF (r = 0.391, p < .001), EF (r = 0.303, p < .001), and total citations (r = 0.323, p < .001). Furthermore, publishers from developed countries exhibited higher mean APC, IF, EF, and citability compared to those from developing countries. The author argues that these findings expose a structural inequality in global science: high-impact, GOA journals create a 'pay-to-play' model where prestige, citations, and credibility are purchased rather than earned, disadvantaging researchers from developing countries, unaffiliated independent scholars, and those in conservation-critical fields. The study highlights the paradox where the very mechanisms of open access (higher citation counts, higher visibility) are gated behind costs that exclude the most resource-constrained contributors, potentially suppressing important research—particularly in tropical ecology and conservation—that cannot access the >1000 USD fees required by prestigious GOA outlets.

fragment: This study addresses the limitations of RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2 diagnosis, where only 47-59% of positive cases were identified due to low viral load, sampling timing, or mutations. The authors developed a multiplex-PCR method using 343 pairs of specific primers (172 in the first pool, 171 in the second overlapping pool) targeting the entire SARS-CoV-2 genome. Mathematical modeling established that while RT-PCR detects 4.8 copies at 95% probability, the single 172-primer panel detects 1.15 copies, and combining both pools yields 0.29 copies at 95% probability. Experimental validation using S and N gene plasmids spiked into human RNA confirmed detection from 8,900 down to 2.8 copies, with electrophoretic visualization of library peaks across a dynamic range. In clinical application, 13 nasopharyngeal swab specimens with viral loads from 8 to 675,885 RNA copies/uL were amplified; approximately 95-99% genome coverage at 100X was achieved. Mutations were identified at seven clustered loci, including the D614G variant in 11/13 specimens. A secondary metagenomic multiplex-PCR method using random hexamer-adapters achieved >96% S and N gene coverage with only ~0.6M reads per library, with no host depletion. No cross-reactivity with MERS-CoV, CoV 229E, CoV OC43, CoV NL63, or CoV HKU1 was observed (0% read alignment).

fragment:
This paper introduces BATI, a novel Bayesian rare variant association test using Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (INLA) for the association of rare genetic variants with complex diseases in case-control study designs. Rare variant association studies (RVAS) face significant power limitations in small-to-medium cohorts when genetic variation explains a small fraction of phenotypic variance. Existing methods such as burden tests (e.g., Burden, SKAT, SKAT-O, KBAC) and variance-component tests (MiST, HBMR) face computational bottlenecks or model-specification trade-offs. BATI overcomes these by employing INLA, a non-sampling-based numerical approximation that estimates full hierarchical Bayesian models of latent Gaussian random fields faster and more accurately than Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), while maintaining the flexibility to integrate arbitrary categorical and numeric variant-specific characteristics as covariates.

The authors benchmark BATI against five existing RVAS tests—Burden, SKAT-O, KBAC, MiST, and HBMR—using realistic semi-synthetic breast cancer cohorts generated by combining thousands of real WES datasets with known ClinVar risk variants. For 8 breast cancer risk genes (including BRCA2, BARD1, CHEK2, PALB2) under 100 simulations each, BATI identifies all risk genes at 0.1% type I error rate (TIER) with >80% power even at 0.5% variance explained (VE), whereas competing methods fail selectively. At 0.01% TIER, BATI identifies all risk genes while Burden, KBAC, and SKAT-O recurrently miss BRCA2; HBMR misses BARD1, CHEK2, and PALB2. The framework is integrated into rvGWAS, a comprehensive RVAS package including quality control, filtering, population structure detection, and multiple association tests. A practical application to a Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia study identified eight candidate predisposition genes including EHMT2 and COPS7A. The work demonstrates that using functional annotation as prior information significantly boosts power without penalizing performance for genes containing mostly missense variants.

fragment: This paper describes the systematic identification, curation, and prioritization of Nipah virus inhibitors (NVIs) through a multi-pronged computational and informatics approach. Nipah virus, a highly pathogenic RNA virus (case fatality rate over 75%) with no approved treatment, is on WHO's R&D Blueprint list of priority diseases. The authors developed the Nipah Virus Inhibitor Knowledgebase (NVIK), an open-access LAMP-based web platform hosting 182 NVI entries, including 98 unique small-molecule inhibitors. Data were mined from 838 PubMed/Google-identified papers and manually curated using a two-person verification system. For prioritization, the authors computed over 1800 (PaDel: 1875) physicochemical descriptors for all NVIs and compared them against 2,346 FDA-approved compounds and 4,644 Enamine antiviral library compounds. A combined evidence strategy was applied: (i) DruLito and PAINS filtering for drug-likeness and toxicity, (ii) assay robustness evaluation (ranking inhibitors based on the quality of identifying assays), and (iii) structural similarity mapping. Of 98 small-molecule NVIs, only a few passed all DruLito filters. Independent assay robustness scoring narrowed the field further. The top 10 NVIs were prioritized based on combined drug-likeness and assay reliability. Notably, EC50/IC50 values as low as 0.47 nM were reported. The study identifies chemical diversity in the NVI set (90 clusters among 98 NVIs) and provides actionable drug repurposing and scaffold discovery leads. The platform allows community submissions to maintain the database.

fragment: This study integrated 3D genome architecture analysis (Hi-C), RNA-seq, and translocation detection in 18 newly diagnosed T-lineage acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) patients and 4 healthy T cell controls to elucidate the role of chromatin organization in T-ALL pathogenesis. The authors found that 3D genome alterations at the compartment, TAD, and loop levels, combined with gene expression profiles, hierarchically classify T-ALL subtypes along the T cell differentiation trajectory. Approximately 29% of differentially expressed genes were associated with 3D structural changes, with upregulated genes enriched in hematopoietic lineage and cell cycle pathways, and downregulated genes in cytokine and TCR signaling. ETP ALL samples, representing an immature differentiation state, were separated from non-ETP ALLs by loop-level structural signatures, showing 1820 enhanced and 831 reduced loops. Adaptation of hic_breakfinder identified 46 translocations, including 34 novel noncoding events, which formed 44 new translocation-mediated loops and drove enhancer hijacking of the HOXA cluster. Two mechanisms were identified: 'cis' enhancer hijacking (e.g., BCL11B-TLX3, TRB-TAL2) and 'trans' gene fusions (e.g., PSIP1-NUP98, SET-NUP214, MLL) activating the HOXA cluster. Hierarchical clustering of HOXA expression revealed that ectopic HOXA11-A13 expression, driven by 5' TAD rearrangements, is associated with double negative and ETP phenotypes, higher JAK-STAT pathway mutations, and poor overall survival in pediatric and young adult T-ALL. HOXA13 positive status emerged as an independent prognostic indicator for overall survival. The study demonstrates that 3D genome rewiring, independent of conventional driver mutations, is a fundamental etiological and prognostic feature of T-ALL differentiation blocking.

fragment:
ProNetView-ccRCC is an interactive, open-access, web-based portal developed to facilitate visual exploration and interpretation of phosphopeptide co-expression networks in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). The platform addresses a critical gap in cancer proteomics: while CPTAC has produced comprehensive proteogenomic data generating complex network models, existing tools are primarily suited for static 2D visualization in print publications rather than user-initiated interactive exploration. 

Built on the Three.js WebGL framework, ProNetView-ccRCC enables 3D interactive visualization of the overall ccRCC phosphopeptide co-expression network comprised of 3,614 genes (representing 20,976 phosphopeptides) and 30 functional pathway-enriched network modules containing at least 20 genes each. The network was constructed using a random-forest based algorithm applied to phosphopeptide-level data from 103 ccRCC samples. 

Key features include: (1) a 3D network exploration interface supporting rotation and zooming; (2) gene/protein querying with automatic highlighting of first-degree neighbors; (3) association querying between phosphopeptide abundance and clinical variables (tumor grade, stage, age, gender) with user-defined FDR cut-offs; (4) pathway enrichment tables with interactive gene lists; and (5) integration with the ProTrack tool for multi-omics heatmap analysis. 

Demonstration examples include the oncogene ERG, which connects to 11 genes within module 26 (Angiogenesis) and maps to 5 peptides, showing a significant association with tumor grade (p-value: 0.003, FDR: 0.118). The portal requires no plugins and runs on all modern web browsers, aiming to lower the computational barrier for the cancer research community to conduct hypothesis-generating analyses on CPTAC ccRCC network data.

fragment: This study presents the first animal model demonstrating spontaneous regression of micro-metastases following surgical excision of the primary tumor (PT) in a triple-negative breast cancer xenograft system. Using MDA-MB-231 HM human breast cancer cells transduced with a highly sensitive firefly luciferase-mCherry reporter in BALB/c nu/nu mice, the authors established an orthotopic model where distant metastases in lymph nodes and lungs emerged spontaneously 2-4 weeks post-tumor implantation. Upon excision of the PT at a metastatic burden of 10⁶ photons/s, the smallest (10⁶ photons/s) metastases exhibited a dramatic signal decrease of up to 100-fold within 24 hours (p<0.0001), while larger metastases (10⁷ photons/s) showed significantly less regression (p<0.000). Sham surgery (tumor spared) produced no regression, confirming the effect is linked to PT removal rather than surgical trauma. In vitro experiments demonstrated that tumor cell-conditioned medium (CM) enhanced cancer cell viability (p<0.001), adhesion (p<0.01), and endothelial tube formation (p<0.0001). In vivo, Alzet osmotic minipumps delivering CM reduced regression by 10-fold compared to serum-free medium (p<0.005). Proteomic analysis (LC-MS, ~2,600 proteins identified) and cytokine array identified IL-8, PDGFaa, Serpin E1 (PAI-1), and MIF as key PT-secreted factors. Concurrent in vivo blockade of these four factors via neutralizing antibodies completely halted metastatic progression (p<0.0001). Retrospective TCGA lung adenocarcinoma analysis confirmed high protein levels of these four factors correlated with significantly lower survival (hazard ratio 2.05, p<0.05). The authors conclude that PT-secreted factors promote early metastatic growth, and the perioperative window offers a therapeutic opportunity to control minimal residual disease by targeting these secreted factors.

fragment:
This study investigates whether global molecular changes in murine macrophage RAW 264.7 cells following activation by CpG DNA or lipopolysaccharide (LPS) are detectable by Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. Using Attenuated Total Reflectance (ATR) FTIR spectroscopy, the authors monitored the molecular composition of macrophages cultured in DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS and 2 mM L-glutamine. Cells were treated with 1 µM K3 ODN (CpG DNA) or 0.5 µg/ml LPS, with measurements taken at 10 min, 30 min, 2 h, and 6 h post-treatment. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) reduced the spectral data (0.5 cm⁻¹ resolution) to two principal components, with PC-1 explaining 83% and PC-2 explaining 11% of the total variability. 

The study reports that CpG DNA and LPS treatment significantly increase total nucleic acid concentration starting from the early time points. RNA synthesis, identified via the 915 cm⁻¹ ribose vibration peak, is prominent up to 2 h post-stimulation, followed by a transition to DNA synthesis from 6 h onwards. For LPS treatment, RNA synthesis is restricted to the first 2 h, consistent with the known pro-inflammatory and anti-proliferative effects of LPS that inhibit DNA synthesis and elicit cell cycle arrest. A rapid increase in total protein (amide I and II bands) is observed for both CpG and LPS treatments, peaking at 10 min–2 h and leveling off or declining thereafter. Furthermore, both CpG and LPS stimulate increased concentrations of fatty acids, triglycerides, and cholesterol (ester C=O stretch near 1741 cm⁻¹ and COO⁻ stretch at 1400 cm⁻¹), suggesting activation of de novo lipogenesis. This work represents the first demonstration of ATR-FTIR spectroscopy as an independent modality to monitor activation dynamics in macrophages post-stimuli, filling a gap where prior 'omics' techniques required extensive sample preparation that could alter chemical ratios.

fragment:
American Foulbrood (AFB), caused by Paenibacillus larvae spores, remains one of the most destructive honeybee diseases. Diagnosis currently relies on subjective, time-consuming visual inspection of capped brood cells, requiring hive dismantling and multiple visits, often missing subclinical or genotype-specific infections. This study presents the 'Foster method,' a novel environmental DNA (eDNA) sampling protocol combining colony entrance swabs with a dual-target qPCR assay (targeting ftsZ and 16S genes) to quantify P. larvae spore levels non-invasively.

Three cohorts of quarantine apiaries across New Zealand were evaluated: 45 hives (8 with clinical AFB) were monitored with nurse bee, entire baseboard, and entrance swabs; 23 hives from one beekeeper yielded 4 clinically positive hives; and a third cohort explored swab pooling.

Key findings include:
1) The dual-target qPCR demonstrated high analytical sensitivity (LOD 4 copies/10 µL), linearity over 7 orders of magnitude (r=0.998), and high amplification efficiency (ftsZ=94%, 16S=96%).
2) The entrance swab method detected equivalent P. larvae levels to entire baseboard swabbing, eliminating the need for hive dismantling.
3) Spore quantities above 565,000 per 10 bees/swab corresponded to a 95% probability of clinical signs.
4) In one instance, a hive without visual signs (Hive 11) showed high spore levels and developed clinical AFB two weeks later, confirming pre-clinical detection.

Statistical analysis (p=0.00) confirmed the strong relationship between increasing spore levels and clinical disease. The Foster method enables rapid, one-time sampling of hives without disruption, with potential scalability to other bee pathogens (Nosema, European foulbrood) and incursion pests (tracheal mites, small hive beetle), transforming AFB surveillance from subjective inspection to quantitative, evidence-based management.

fragment: This paper introduces SPOT-Contact-Single, a protein contact-map prediction method that leverages unsupervised transformer language model embeddings (ESM-1b attention maps) as input features instead of computationally expensive multiple sequence alignments (MSAs). The authors demonstrate that concatenating ESM-1b attention maps with one-hot encoding and SPOT-1D-Single structural features, trained through an ensemble of six ResNet-12 models, significantly outperforms both single-sequence-based predictors (SSCpred) and evolutionary-profile-based predictors (TrRosetta, SPOT-Contact) for proteins with low effective sequence identity (Neff=1). On the CASP14-FM test set, SPOT-Contact-Single achieves a 15% F1-score improvement over SSCpred. On proteins without homologs (Neff=1) in the SPOT-2018 set, it surpasses TrRosetta and SPOT-Contact by 48.7% and 48.5% in F1-score, respectively. The method is not only more accurate for single-sequence contexts but also substantially faster: it runs inference 22-fold faster than TrRosetta on CPU and 42-fold faster on GPU. The architecture employs the Duta et al. (2020) improved ResNet variant with 12 blocks, channel size 64, and kernel size 3. The training set comprises 34,691 proteins, and the method handles the limitation of ESM-1b's 1024 residue sequence window by domain-wise prediction.

fragment: EcoEvoApps is an open-source R package (ecoevoapps) and associated website providing 11 interactive Shiny apps that simulate fundamental models in ecology and evolutionary biology. The initiative addresses a documented gap in EEB education where the language of mathematical modeling remains inaccessible to empirically-trained researchers and students, contributing to lower citation rates of quantitative papers and poorer student evaluations of quantitative courses. The package includes models selected from undergraduate syllabi and standard textbooks (Gotelli 2008; Begon and Townsend 2020), covering resource competition, predator-prey dynamics, and more. A core set of nine apps is available in English, Spanish, Chinese, Turkish, and Portuguese. Methodologically, the package is built on R's Shiny framework, using run_ functions for model simulation and plot_ functions for ggplot2 visualization. A classroom evaluation with 51 students at UCLA showed that 40/51 students (78.4%) rated the apps as moderately to very helpful for understanding models as a whole. Further surveys at the University of Missouri confirmed gains in student confidence in models, particularly among students with higher interest in related topics. The package is entirely open-source and written in R, distinguishing it from existing web resources by allowing customization and local deployment. The authors plan to expand into evolutionary biology and population genetics models and develop formalized lesson plans for educators.

fragment: This study investigates the signaling mechanism of Cellular Communication Network Factor 2 (CCN2/CTGF) in primary cultured lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). The authors demonstrate that CCN2 upregulates lymphatic endothelial markers (Lyve1, Podoplanin, Prox1) and lymphangiogenic factors (Vegfc, Vegfd, Flt4) in a dose-dependent manner up to 100 ng/mL, while not affecting Kdr expression. A phospho-receptor tyrosine kinase array revealed that CCN2 does not activate VEGFR2 or VEGFR3, suggesting signaling proceeds through an alternative receptor complex. Phospho-ERK was significantly increased (p<0.001) by CCN2, but not so were p38 MAPK, JNK, AKT, NFkB, or Smad proteins. Integrin analysis showed that Itgav, Itga9, and Itgb1 are predominantly expressed in LECs, and CCN2-induced phospho-ERK was partially decreased by siRNA knockdown of integrin av (p=0.0040) but not by integrin a9 knockdown. Interestingly, integrin b1 suppression increased phospho-ERK without CCN2 stimulation (p=0.05), but CCN2 did not further alter phosphorylation in b1-depleted cells. A cell growth assay revealed that CCN2 weakly suppressed LEC proliferation at 24 h (p=0.003 for 50 ng/mL; p=0.02 for 100 ng/mL), contrasting with the in vivo Matrigel plug assay where CCN2 promoted Podoplanin-positive vessel formation and tubular structures. Immunoprecipitation demonstrated that CCN2 enhances the binding of ERK and DUSP6, and DUSP6 knockdown increased CCN2-induced phospho-ERK at multiple time points (p<0.001 at 15 min, p=0.004 at 48 h). In vivo Matrigel plugs showed significantly increased Podoplanin-positive vessels, phospho-ERK, and DUSP6 in CCN2-supplemented gels compared to controls (p<0.05). The authors conclude that CCN2-related lymphangiogenesis is regulated by DUSP6, which acts as a negative modulator of ERK signaling, and that the integrin av-ERK-DUSP6 axis may represent a therapeutic target in head and neck cancers associated with CCN2 over-expression.

fragment: This study investigates the non-canonical role of tumor-expressed PD-L1 (tPD-L1) in immune evasion, demonstrating that tPD-L1 does not directly protect tumor cells from cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) lysis but instead exerts its suppressive function through an intermediate myeloid-cell-mediated pathway. Using 4T1 (TNBC) and CT26 (MMRp CRC) murine cancer models, the authors show that while tPD-L1 loss does not affect primary tumor growth or the initial seeding of disseminated tumor cells to the lung, it significantly reduces lung metastasis in a CTL-dependent manner. Single-cell RNA sequencing of 4T1-colonized lungs revealed that tPD-L1 engages PD-1 on myeloid cells (mPD-1), suppressing type I interferon (IFN-I) and STAT1 signaling. This suppression reduces expression of the CTL-recruiting chemokines Cxcl9 and Cxcl10, creating a cold immunological niche that impairs CTL recruitment to lung metastases. In vitro co-culture experiments with RAW264.7 macrophages confirmed that tPD-L1/mPD-1 engagement enhances SHP-2 activation, decreases pSTAT1, and reduces MHC class II expression. Myeloid cell depletion via clodronate liposomes abolished the tPD-L1-mediated promotion of lung metastasis, confirming the essential role of the myeloid compartment. In human patients with metastatic basal cell carcinoma treated with PD-1 blockade, myeloid cell PHATE analysis demonstrated that PD-1 blockade releases differentiation restriction, enhances IFN-I signaling, and increases CTL-recruiting chemokines. The study proposes the tPD-L1/mPD-1/IFN-I/STAT1/Cxcl9/10 axis as a key mechanism controlling CTL infiltration in metastatic niches, with implications for neoadjuvant and adjuvant ICB therapy.

fragment:
This paper proposes and validates a bidirectional Long Short Term Memory (bi-LSTM) network architecture for decoding brain states from functional MRI (fMRI) data, specifically addressing the temporal dynamics of the Blood Oxygen Level Dependent (BOLD) response. Conventional LSTM models capture information only from past time points, but due to inherent latency and BOLD response dynamics, the authors argue that future temporal context is also critical. The proposed bi-LSTM processes fMRI time-series in both forward and reverse directions, collating hidden activations to form a dual-directional 'memory' that predicts brain states at every time instance without requiring pre-processing delay adjustments. The framework was validated on working memory task fMRI data from the Human Connectome Project (HCP), using 400 participants performing a 2-back task across four stimulus categories (tools, places, faces, body parts) and a 0-back control. Data was preprocessed into 360 cortical regions of interest, yielding 405 time-points per scan, yielding S=9 brain states (including fixation blocks labeled as 'others'). The bi-LSTM model (two hidden layers with 256 units each) was compared against a unidirectional LSTM (same specifications) and a three-layer feed-forward neural network. Using inter-subject 10-fold cross-validation (N=360 for training, N=40 for testing), the bi-LSTM-c (vector concatenation) achieved 0.84 ± 0.02 accuracy, compared to 0.66 ± 0.18 for the unidirectional LSTM, an absolute improvement of 0.18 (approximately +27% relative). The bi-LSTM required no time-delay adjustment for BOLD response synchronization, unlike prior methods that assumed a constant response delay across all voxels. The study concludes that future temporal context contains useful information for BOLD dynamics and that the bi-LSTM framework provides a robust, delay-free solution for brain-state decoding in fMRI.

Key findings indicate that the bi-LSTM consistently outperforms its unidirectional counterpart across all brain states, with the unidirectional model exhibiting higher misclassification rates. The highest confusion for both models occurred for the 'Others' (fixation) class, and the second-highest confusion involved mislabeling stimulus-specific tasks as the base task. The model also occasionally confused 'body' and 'tools' stimuli. Limitations noted include the fixed windowing approach, the remaining challenge of class imbalance, and the need for further analysis of cortical regions confused between stimuli categories. The work establishes the bi-LSTM as a viable alternative to traditional univariate and multivariate decoding methods in sequential brain-state analysis.

fragment: This study presents a comprehensive phylogenomic reassessment of three closely related thermophilic genera within the family Bacillaceae—Anoxybacillus, Geobacillus, and Parageobacillus—using 113 publicly available whole-genome sequences. The primary methodological framework integrated three complementary phylogenomic metrics: a maximum-likelihood core-gene tree derived from 662 orthologous genes, Average Nucleotide Identity (ANI), and Average Amino Acid Identity (AAI) dendrograms. The core gene tree revealed a fundamental phylogenetic split into two main clades: Clade I, containing all Geobacillus, all Parageobacillus, and a subset of Anoxybacillus species; and Clade II, containing the majority of Anoxybacillus species. Clade I was further resolved into three distinct sub-clades corresponding to Geobacillus, Parageobacillus, and a third clade (I-c) composed of Anoxybacillus tepidamans and one unnamed genomospecies. The authors propose that clade I-c be elevated to the new genus Quasigeobacillus gen. nov., supported by 6 unique coding sequence (CDS) identifiers and a position consistently distinct from the three established genera across all three phylogenetic methods. Two Anoxybacillus species (A. vitaminiphilus and A. amylolyticus) showed inconsistent positioning and remain unresolved. The study concludes that taxonomical circumscription based on isolated genus analysis is insufficient; closely related genera must be considered together in phylogenomic workflows to avoid incongruent taxonomic assignments for new strains.

fragment: This study provides two cryo-EM structures of endogenously phosphorylated Saccharomyces cerevisiae Ycf1 (a glutathione transporter of the ABC-C subfamily) at 3.4Å and 4.0Å resolution, capturing previously unobserved ordered states of the intrinsically disordered regulatory R-domain (residues 901-935) in two inward-facing conformations (IFwide and IFnarrow). The R-domain, phosphorylated at S908, T911, and S914, is shown to be helical at its C-terminus (residues 920-929) and forms extensive electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions with NBD1 (spanning three buried hydrophobic sites) and the lasso domain. Biochemical data, including ATPase assays, in-gel phosphoprotein staining, limited proteolysis, and LC-MS/MS, confirm that R-domain phosphorylation reorganizes the Ycf1 architecture and is required for maximal ATPase activity. The dephosphorylated state shows a more complete protease digestion pattern and drastically reduced ATPase activity, consistent with cellular phenotypes where S908 and T911 mutations impair cadmium detoxification. The R-domain encircles NBD1 in both structures, with the IFwide-to-IFnarrow transition involving a rigid body movement of the R-domain/NBD1 complex relative to NBD2 and a reconfiguration of the ATP-binding sites, including partial occlusion of the non-functional ATP site in NBD1. The R-domain phosphorylation sites align with PKA-like (RRAS) and CKII kinase recognition motifs. A conserved inhibitory phosphosite at S251 (lasso domain) is identified in proximity, poised to disrupt the R-domain interaction via electrostatic repulsion. These findings challenge existing models of R-domain disordered-to-ordered transition and provide mechanistic insights for the ABCC transporter family, with clinical relevance to CFTR and lumacaftor binding.

fragment: This study provides two cryo-EM structures of endogenously phosphorylated Saccharomyces cerevisiae Ycf1 (a glutathione transporter of the ABC-C subfamily) at 3.4Å and 4.0Å resolution, capturing previously unobserved ordered states of the intrinsically disordered regulatory R-domain (residues 901-935) in two inward-facing conformations (IFwide and IFnarrow). The R-domain, phosphorylated at S908, T911, and S914, is shown to be helical at its C-terminus (residues 920-929) and forms extensive electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions with NBD1 (spanning three buried hydrophobic sites) and the lasso domain. Biochemical data, including ATPase assays, in-gel phosphoprotein staining, limited proteolysis, and LC-MS/MS, confirm that R-domain phosphorylation reorganizes the Ycf1 architecture and is required for maximal ATPase activity. The dephosphorylated state shows a more complete protease digestion pattern and drastically reduced ATPase activity, consistent with cellular phenotypes where S908 and T911 mutations impair cadmium detoxification. The R-domain encircles NBD1 in both structures, with the IFwide-to-IFnarrow transition involving a rigid body movement of the R-domain/NBD1 complex relative to NBD2 and a reconfiguration of the ATP-binding sites, including partial occlusion of the non-functional ATP site in NBD1. The R-domain phosphorylation sites align with PKA-like (RRAS) and CKII kinase recognition motifs. A conserved inhibitory phosphosite at S251 (lasso domain) is identified in proximity, poised to disrupt the R-domain interaction via electrostatic repulsion. These findings challenge existing models of R-domain disordered-to-ordered transition and provide mechanistic insights for the ABCC transporter family, with clinical relevance to CFTR and lumacaftor binding.

fragment: This study evaluated the interaction between seed treatment with plant growth regulators (PGRs) and nitrogen fertilization on the germination, dry matter yield, and physiological composition of Brachiaria decumbens cv. Basilisk. The experiment was conducted in two stages: (1) a germination and initial growth assay (30 DAS) using coated versus conventional seeds with four PGR levels (0, 8, 16, 24 mL·kg⁻¹), and (2) a growth and fertilization experiment with four N application methods. Coated seeds exhibited higher germination percentages and speed index regardless of PGR treatment. A quadratic effect of PGR on germination identified 10.3 mL·kg⁻¹ as the optimal concentration for germination, while 12.8 mL·kg⁻¹ optimized root dry mass. A significant interaction between seed type and PGR level was found for leaf and pseudostem dry mass; coated seeds performed best at 0 and 8.0 mL·kg⁻¹ (optimal at 8.85 and 9.57 mL·kg⁻¹ respectively), while conventional seeds required higher concentrations (15.5 and 18.1 mL·kg⁻¹) for comparable yields. Soil N-fertilization consistently increased dry mass of all plant structures and root volume, with the highest yields achieved when PGR and soil fertilization were combined. Root dry mass increased only under combined PGR and multiple fertilization. Chlorophyll a was significantly increased by PGR, and foliar N-fertilization increased chlorophyll a, b, total chlorophyll, and carotenoids. The study concludes that low-level PGR treatment in coated seeds and soil N-fertilization are effective strategies for enhancing Brachiaria establishment, with PGR acting via hormonal signaling networks and N-fertilization maximizing photosynthetic rates.

fragment: This prospective registry study investigated whether chronic total occlusion (CTO) lesion length significantly affects six-month angiographic and two-year clinical outcomes following successful percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with drug-eluting stents (DES). A total of 235 consecutive CTO patients undergoing successful DES PCI between November 2004 and October 2010 at Korea University Guro Hospital were divided into long CTO (≥30mm, n=159) and short CTO (<30mm, n=76) groups. The study aimed to determine if lesion length serves as a prognostic factor in the DES era, given prior evidence that long coronary lesions correlate with worse PCI outcomes. Baseline characteristics were similar except for higher prior PCI in the long group and more frequent bifurcation lesions in the short group. In-hospital complications were similar except for more frequent intimal dissection in the long group. At six months, angiographic outcomes, including binary restenosis (19.1% vs. 8.8%, p=0.12) and in-stent restenosis (33.3% vs. 26.6%, p=0.42), showed no statistically significant difference between groups, though a numerical trend toward worse outcomes in long CTO was observed. At two years, hard clinical endpoints—total death (3.1% vs. 5.2%, p=0.43), cardiac death (1.2% vs. 2.6%, p=0.45), MI (1.8% vs. 2.6%, p=0.71), and MACE (21.3% vs. 13.1%, p=0.13)—were statistically similar. However, the long CTO group had significantly higher repeat PCI (18.8% vs. 7.8%, p<0.05) and TVR (16.3% vs. 6.5%, p<0.05). Multivariate logistic regression identified long CTO as a significant independent predictor for repeat PCI (OR 4.26; CI 1.53-11.9; p=0.006) and TVR (OR 4.23; CI 1.52-11.8; p<0.05). The authors conclude that while long CTO lesion length predicts higher revascularization rates, it does not translate into worse hard endpoints in the DES era, and long-term, larger-scale studies are needed to confirm.

fragment:
This paper is a critical rebuttal by King et al. against a bioRxiv preprint by Brüschweiler et al. regarding the mitochondrial ADP/ATP carrier (AAC3) of yeast. Brüschweiler et al. claimed that AAC3 could be refolded from Escherichia coli inclusion bodies to homogeneity in the detergent dodecyl-phosphocholine (DPC) and maintained in a folded, active state for ITC and NMR studies. King et al. systematically refute these claims using thermostability assays, ITC, and functional reconstitution experiments. They demonstrate that DPC, rather than stabilizing AAC3, causes immediate loss of tertiary structure and inactivation upon isolation from the inner mitochondrial membrane. 

Key evidence includes: 1) ITC measurements showing a CATR binding Kd of ~15 μM for DPC-refolded AAC3, versus 72 nM for native AAC3 in dodecyl-maltoside/tetraoleoyl cardiolipin (a 200–2000-fold difference); 2) thermostability assays using CPM fluorescence showing that while mild detergents support a typical protein melt curve, DPC yields no transition, indicating a non-native, unfolded state; 3) functional reconstitution assays where prior dilution into DPC caused complete loss of CATR-sensitive ADP uptake in proteoliposomes. The authors further note that the ADP binding Kd (500 μM) and CATR chemical shift perturbations reported by Brüschweiler et al. are inconsistent with known membrane-bound values and established structural data. They conclude the DPC-refolded AAC3 data lacks biological relevance, as the detergent is harsh enough to denature functional carrier protein.

fragment: This study provides the first evidence that the sarco/endoplasmic reticulum calcium-ATPase (SERCA) regulates paramyxovirus replication of Peste des petits ruminants virus (PPRV) and Newcastle disease virus (NDV). Using a library of chemical inhibitors, Thapsigargin was identified as a SERCA-specific inhibitor that significantly reduces NDV and PPRV replication in Vero cells at a non-cytotoxic concentration of 0.5 µM. Conversely, overexpression of SERCA2 in HeLa/goat kidney cells rescued the inhibitory effect of Thapsigargin, confirming a supportive role for SERCA in viral replication. Time-of-addition and virus step-specific assays revealed that Thapsigargin specifically impairs viral entry and intracellular localization rather than attachment, RNA synthesis, or budding. Immunofluorescence showed that Thapsigargin treatment caused ~70% of cells to exhibit defective cytoplasmic foci of viral proteins instead of surface localization. Notably, NDV acquired significant but incomplete resistance to Thapsigargin on long-term passage (70 passages), with ~100-fold inhibition at P35, while PPRV showed no such resistance. The authors report this as a rare example of a virus acquiring resistance to an inhibitor targeting a cellular host factor, expanding on the precedent set by CVB3/PI4KIIIα and HCV/CsA. The study identifies SERCA as a novel proviral host factor and a candidate drug target for broad-spectrum paramyxovirus antivirals.

fragment: This study characterizes the transcriptional regulation and clinical significance of MicroRNA-196a (MIR196A) in estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer. MIR196A, transcribed from two genomic loci (HOXC/MIR196A2 and HOXB/MIR196A1), displays complex expression patterns where MIR196A2 expression highly correlates with HOXC genes, particularly HOXC10, in breast tumours but shows more restricted association with HOXC11/10 in normal breast tissue. The authors demonstrate that MIR196A2 is transcriptionally regulated by estrogen via ERα binding to two putative promoter regions (PP1 and PP3) upstream of the transcription start site, with PP1 (the HOXC10 promoter) showing the highest luciferase activity. Long-range transcriptional regulation is mediated by two major interacting elements: a previously identified HOTAIR distal enhancer (HDE) and a novel interacting partner (MIR196A2-Enhancer, mE), both of which physically interact with the MIR196A2/HOXC10 promoter region as confirmed by ChIA-PET and 3C-qPCR. In clinical samples from the METABRIC cohort, high MIR196A expression is significantly over-expressed in breast tumours compared to normal tissue, correlates with increased tumour stage, and serves as a robust prognostic factor: high expression is associated with poor survival in advanced and post-menopausal ER+ disease but better outcome in triple-negative breast cancer. The prognostic impact is state-dependent; in premenopausal women, high MIR196A expression paradoxically associates with good ER+ outcome (one of the few significant biomarkers in this subgroup), whereas in post-menopausal women, high expression predicts poor outcome. Therapeutic resistance further drives MIR196A elevation, with expression significantly increased in tamoxifen-resistant (TAMR) but almost depleted in fulvestrant-resistant (FASR) MCF7 cells, as well as in paclitaxel and adromycin-resistant lines. ERα ChIP-Seq in human patient samples reveals increased ERα occupancy at MIR196A enhancer and promoter regions in non-responders and metastases, suggesting that enhancer over-activation drives therapeutic resistance.

fragment: This study investigates whether conspecific negative density-dependence (CNDD), a proposed mechanism for regulating species coexistence and diversity, operates on seedling establishment of Quercus costaricensis, a monodominant oak in the Talamanca highland forests of Costa Rica. The authors tested the importance of CNDD regulation on seedling survival and recruitment of 3,538 seedlings monitored between 2014 and 2017 at the Cerro de la Muerte Biological Station (3100-3350 m a.s.l.). Using spatial statistics (univariate Ripley's K) and generalized linear mixed-effects models with binomial and quasi-Poisson distributions, they examined the effects of conspecific seedling density, distance to the nearest adult, herbivory intensity, and bamboo (Chusquea spp.) density on annual survival. Contrary to the Janzen-Connell hypothesis, no significant effect of CNDD was found on seedling survival; annual survival remained high (above 63% per year). Instead, herbivory and bamboo density significantly reduced survival. Herbivory paradoxically decreased at higher seedling densities, and seedling survival was highest at intermediate distances from adults, consistent with positive adult facilitation via ectomycorrhizal transfer. In recruitment analyses, seedling recruitment significantly increased with conspecific seedling density but was independent of adult or bamboo density. The authors argue that predator satiation and adult facilitation explain the absence of CNDD, contributing to the species' extreme dominance (>90% of basal stem area) in montane forests. The results challenge the universality of CNDD and suggest that dominant, masting tropical species may escape density-dependent mortality through life-history traits, predator satiation, and mutualistic facilitation.

fragment: This study investigates whether conspecific negative density-dependence (CNDD), a proposed mechanism for regulating species coexistence and diversity, operates on seedling establishment of Quercus costaricensis, a monodominant oak in the Talamanca highland forests of Costa Rica. The authors tested the importance of CNDD regulation on seedling survival and recruitment of 3,538 seedlings monitored between 2014 and 2017 at the Cerro de la Muerte Biological Station (3100-3350 m a.s.l.). Using spatial statistics (univariate Ripley's K) and generalized linear mixed-effects models with binomial and quasi-Poisson distributions, they examined the effects of conspecific seedling density, distance to the nearest adult, herbivory intensity, and bamboo (Chusquea spp.) density on annual survival. Contrary to the Janzen-Connell hypothesis, no significant effect of CNDD was found on seedling survival; annual survival remained high (above 63% per year). Instead, herbivory and bamboo density significantly reduced survival. Herbivory paradoxically decreased at higher seedling densities, and seedling survival was highest at intermediate distances from adults, consistent with positive adult facilitation via ectomycorrhizal transfer. In recruitment analyses, seedling recruitment significantly increased with conspecific seedling density but was independent of adult or bamboo density. The authors argue that predator satiation and adult facilitation explain the absence of CNDD, contributing to the species' extreme dominance (>90% of basal stem area) in montane forests. The results challenge the universality of CNDD and suggest that dominant, masting tropical species may escape density-dependent mortality through life-history traits, predator satiation, and mutualistic facilitation.

fragment: This study evaluates the acute toxicity of six engineered nanoparticles (Ag, Au, CuO, ZnO, TiO2, SiO2) and three soluble salts (CuSO4, ZnSO4, AgNO3) on Artemia sp. cysts and hatched nauplii. The authors established two complementary assays: (1) a hatching rate assay where hydrated cysts were exposed to nanoparticles at 100 mg/L and 10 mg/L in 25% salt water, measuring hatching rate (fully hatched motile nauplii/total cysts) after 24 hours, and (2) a standard Artemia toxicity test (ARC protocol) where 10 normally hatched nauplii were exposed to concentrations ranging from 0.01 to 100 mg/L, measuring mortality over 48 hours. Physicochemical characterization via TEM and DLS revealed that nanoparticles exhibited reduced size and altered dispersion behavior in salt water compared to MilliQ water, with visible flocculation for CuO and ZnO. Key results showed that Ag and CuO NPs were the most toxic; Ag NPs at 100 mg/L reduced hatching to ~29% with only 50% viability, and in the larval test, the LC50 of Ag NPs was ~10.12 mg/L at 24 hours. The study established a toxicity order of Ag > CuO > ZnO > Au > TiO2 > SiO2. A strong inverse correlation (r = -0.7853) was found between hatching rate reduction and larval mortality, suggesting that hatching rate can serve as a valid surrogate endpoint. Oxidative stress was confirmed via DCFDA staining, showing ROS accumulation primarily in Ag-exposed nauplii and their guts. The study concludes that Artemia sp. are a robust, cost-effective model for high-throughput nanoparticle hazard identification, with hatching tests providing an efficient pre-screening alternative to standard lethality assays.
